 Order

Per: Sanjay Dwivedi, J.
This first application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.104/2024 registered at Police Station- Ashta, District- Sehore, for the offence under Sections 218, 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 29.06.2024.

He submits that as per the case of the prosecution, the Society in which the applicant is only a Member,
moved an application for granting affiliation and recognition for running the nursing college giving false information about the strength of the college and hospital; when this fact was enquired about by the Special Agency, it was ultimately found incorrect and as such, by giving incorrect information, affiliation and recognition have been obtained and, therefore, offence got registered.
He further submits that there is 2 MCRC-29306-2024 no direct allegation or any individual role ascribed against the present applicant.

He submits that the application was made by the Society signed by the President and Secretary of the same but the present applicant was not aware of the facts of the application, therefore, in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and looking to the period of custody and also the role assigned to the applicant, he is entitled to be released on bail.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and submits that it was a joint effort of the society and merely because the present applicant is only a Member of the Dr. Harsih Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16775161/
1 Society, he cannot be given clean chit and it cannot be said that the applicant was not aware of the fact as to what the Society is doing.

sentences.text: He submits that this application deserves to be rejected.

4. Considering the aforesaid, perusal of case-diary, looking to the nature of allegations made against the applicant, the role assigned and also the period of custody, though the bail application has been opposed by learned counsel for the State, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, we are inclined to consider and allow this bail application.

5. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.
6. On being released on bail, the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
